title: Checkpoint: Exploring the Ocean
objective: After this level you can trace how people explored the ocean, from sailing ships to submersibles.
summary: From canoes and star compasses to Challenger, scuba, Trieste and satellites, and a wayfinder who sailed the old way home in 1980.

cards.headline: From stars to satellites: how did people get to know the ocean?
cards.body: This chapter crossed thousands of years in canoes, ships, helmets and subs. Put it in order, then meet a navigator who proved the oldest way still works.

events.label: Voyagers have settled Hawaiʻi, Rapa Nui and Aotearoa
Harrison's H4 goes to sea: longitude by clock
HMS Challenger sounds the deep and finds 4,700+ new species
TOPEX/Poseidon starts measuring sea level from orbit

cards.fact: In 1980, Nainoa Thompson navigated Hōkūleʻa from Tahiti to Hawaiʻi without instruments.
cards.context: The Polynesian Voyaging Society says it was a feat that hadn't been accomplished in 600 years. Thompson had learned from Mau Piailug of Satawal, who sailed along in support. Level 82's star compass wasn't a museum piece. It went back to sea.

mascot.line: Six hundred years between trips, and the stars were right where the navigators left them.

cards.headline: Two problems: distance and depth
cards.body: Every explorer here fought distance or depth. Distance gave way to stars and then clocks: latitude from a star's height, longitude from home time at 15° per hour. Depth was harder, because pressure climbs one atmosphere every 10 m. Scuba answers it by matching the water's pressure with a demand regulator. Trieste shut it out, keeping its crew inside a heavy steel cabin built to resist the deep.

questions.prompt: Exploring the Ocean recap: a scuba regulator and Trieste's steel cabin both deal with deep-water pressure. How do they differ?

options.label: Both keep their people at the surface's pressure
options.rationale: Scuba does the opposite: it matches the water.

options.label: Scuba removes the pressure; Trieste adds more of it
options.rationale: Neither removes or adds pressure that way.

options.label: Only Trieste had to deal with any pressure at all
Scuba matches the water's pressure; the cabin resists it

questions.explanation: A demand regulator gives air at the water's pressure; Trieste's heavy steel cabin kept the deep's pressure out.
